transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. 

Um... well, I'm mostly just here because of a little issue at work. I always try to do a really good job—I'm a cashier—but... I guess I've been getting a little stuck lately? Like, doing things that don't quite fit the moment. I don't want to make it sound like a huge problem, but sometimes I'll catch myself tapping the scanner in a little pattern, or... or I'll just sort of freeze with my hand hovering over the cash drawer while a customer is waiting. 

It's silly, really, probably just a bad habit, but... well, my manager actually wrote me up for it last week. I felt terrible about it, I really don't want to be an inconvenience to the customers or my boss. I just want to get it fixed so I can do things right... does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you can help me with?
Before you tap the scanner in that pattern, do you notice a specific worry or uncomfortable feeling that builds up, which then gets relieved once you complete the tapping?

Oh, um... no, not really. I hope that's okay to say. It's not like I'm anxious or, you know, worried about something bad happening if I don't do it. I know some people get like that, but for me... it just sort of happens? 

I don't really feel a buildup of anything beforehand, and I definitely don't feel relieved afterward. Honestly, I mostly just feel a little embarrassed when I realize I'm doing it, especially if a customer is watching me. I really hope I'm explaining this right... is that helpful at all? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so I'm not wasting your time.

When you notice yourself tapping in that pattern or freezing with your hand over the drawer, do you feel like you could stop yourself right away if you tried, or does it feel like it happens on its own before you even realize it?

Um, well... I really try my best to stay focused, you know? I want to be a good employee. But... honestly, it feels like it just happens on its own before I even realize it. 

Like I was saying before, about getting stuck doing things that don't fit the moment? The tapping the scanner in a pattern, or... or when I freeze with my hand just hovering over the cash drawer while the customer is standing right there waiting. I don't mean to do it at all. It's just... suddenly I'm doing it, and then I realize I'm doing it, and that's when I try to stop. 

But by then, the customer has usually noticed, and... well, that's why I got written up last week. I really, really don't want to be a bother to anyone, and I know it probably sounds so strange. I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is... does that make sense? Am I explaining it okay?

Aside from the scanner tapping and the freezing with your hand over the drawer, have you noticed any other repeated movements—like blinking, head jerking—or any sounds or noises you make without meaning to?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I really try to be mindful of how I present myself, especially at the store, so I definitely haven't noticed making any noises or... or jerking my head or anything like that. 

I really hope that's okay, that I don't have that to report? It's really just the, um, the tapping and the freezing with my hands that I mentioned before. I try so hard to be polite and quiet otherwise, so I think I would notice if I was making sounds. I hope I'm giving you the information you need... is that the right kind of answer? I just want to make sure I'm doing this correctly for you.
Can you tell me how long you've been noticing this tapping and freezing behavior—did it start recently, or have you had similar repetitive movements since you were a child?

Um... well, it definitely hasn't been since I was a child. I've always tried to be very put-together, you know? I was always a very quiet, well-behaved kid. I wouldn't want you to think I've always struggled with things like this. 

It's really just been... maybe the last three months? That's when I started noticing the tapping and the freezing up at the register. And, well... I guess that's also when I started noticing the other things, too. Like... um... sometimes hearing things that maybe other people aren't hearing? The voices, I mean. And just those moments where I feel like I'm doing things that are a little out of place for the situation. 

But it's only been about three months, I promise. It's relatively new, and I'm really hoping it's just a temporary thing, maybe just some stress? I really hope that's an okay answer. Is three months what you were looking for? I just want to be as helpful as I can.

During these past three months, have you also noticed changes in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or on the other hand, unusually energetic or elated—that occurred around the same time as the voices and freezing?

Oh, um... no, I don't believe so. I really try my best to keep a positive attitude, you know? Even with the... the other things happening, I definitely haven't felt hopeless or depressed. I wouldn't want you to think I'm letting myself get down like that. 

And I haven't been overly energetic or disruptive either. I try to stay pretty even-keeled so I can do my job properly and not bother anyone. So my mood has been pretty normal, I think. 

I really hope that's a good sign? I mean, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on. Is it okay that my mood has been fine? I hope I'm not complicating things for you by not having those symptoms.
Have you had any recent medical illnesses, neurological problems, head injuries, or new medication/substance use in the past few months around when these symptoms started?

Oh, no. No, nothing like that. I... I try to take really good care of my physical health, you know? So I haven't been sick, and I definitely haven't hit my head or had any kind of... well, any physical injuries at all. 

And as for medications or, um, substances... no, absolutely not. I don't do anything like that. I wouldn't want to do anything that could jeopardize my job at the store, so I've always been very clean that way. I wouldn't want you to think I was mixed up in anything bad. 

I really hope that helps rule some things out for you? I know sometimes people might take things they shouldn't, but I promise I haven't started any new medications or anything else. Is it a good thing that my physical health is okay? I just want to make sure I'm being as helpful as possible for your notes.
Can you tell me more about the voices you've been hearing—do they talk about you as if discussing you with someone else, comment on what you're doing, or tell you to do things?

Um... well, I really want to assure you that they don't tell me to do anything bad. I would never listen to anything like that, I promise. I've always been a very gentle person. It's mostly just... well, most days I hear what sounds like a couple of people talking, just sort of off to the side of me. 

It's usually just about work. Sometimes I'll hear them calling my name from the stockroom, or... or they'll say I rang something up wrong at the register. But then I turn around to apologize or see what they need, and there’s nobody there. And I've noticed that no one else around me heard it either. 

I really try my best to just keep smiling and keep working when it happens, because I want to be a good employee and not make a fuss. I hope that doesn't make me sound... you know, too strange? Is it a better sign that they just talk about normal work things instead of telling me what to do? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of details.
